Conclude the meeting without documenting decisions, action items, responsible parties, or timelines, trusting participants to remember outcomes.

explanation: Effective feedback sessions require structure, preparation, and documentation to ensure clarity and accountability. Option B establishes clear expectations through advance preparation, enables informed discussion, and creates a written record that prevents misunderstandings and ensures follow-through. Options A and D rely on memory, which leads to lost context and missed accountability. Option C forces participants to engage with materials in real time without preparation, reducing the quality of feedback and discussion.

question: A customer-service agent system has expanded from 12 tools to 40 tools across 24 months. Performance metrics show a decline in routing accuracy from 89 percent to 76 percent, and tool-selection latency has increased by 2.8 seconds per request. An engineer proposes inserting a filtering agent upstream to reduce the visible tool set per request. Which two findings would support a capability reorganization strategy instead? Each correct answer provides a key insight. (Select two.)

options.text: Multiple tools have overlapping descriptions that create ambiguity across different service categories.
Several tools have remained unused throughout the past 120 days of production traffic.
The 40 tools align with five distinct customer-service domains within the agent's operational scope.
Tool-router patterns are extensively documented in open-source agent frameworks.
A filtering agent would add an extra model invocation to every incoming request.

explanation: Option A supports reorganization because overlapping descriptions indicate poor capability boundaries that should be restructured into clearer, non-overlapping categories. Option C supports reorganization because the natural alignment with five distinct domains suggests the tools should be reorganized into domain-specific agents or capability groups rather than filtered. Option B (unused tools) would be addressed by simple removal, not reorganization. Option E describes a drawback of the filtering approach but doesn't support reorganization as an alternative strategy. Option D is irrelevant to choosing between filtering versus reorganization.

question: A document classification system has been live for eight months. A user reported that a classified document was assigned to an incorrect category with high confidence. The engineering team needs to determine whether this represents a systemic issue or a one-time occurrence. Which two Diligence-competency actions should you take? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. (Select two.)

options.text: Analyze a representative batch of recent classifications to assess the error rate and prevalence across the user base.
Immediately shut down the system for all users without conducting any preliminary investigation or root-cause analysis.
Examine whether validation or confidence-filtering mechanisms are present in the classification pipeline.
Assure users that the classifier will never produce misclassifications due to how the system was built.
Assume the issue is isolated and proceed without any additional investigation or monitoring.

explanation: When a potential defect surfaces in a deployed system, you must both quantify its scope and assess whether architectural safeguards exist. Option A is correct because sampling recent outputs establishes whether the problem is widespread or truly isolated, which informs whether architectural changes are needed. Option C is correct because reviewing the pipeline for validation controls (such as confidence thresholds or human review gates) determines whether the system has built-in protections and where improvements should be made. Options B and E represent the extremes of over-reaction and under-reaction respectively, while Option D makes an unfounded guarantee that contradicts the observed failure.

question: An engineer working with Claude Code encounters an access denied error when attempting an operation that should be permitted. Which approach best resolves the issue?

options.text: Have the engineer repeat the same operation multiple times until the denial ceases, without examining the permission configuration to understand whether the restriction is intentional.
Remove all permission constraints across the entire system to eliminate the denial, discarding all tool-pattern and rule-based controls rather than targeting the specific rule.

Examine the permission rules at all configuration levels—system-wide, command-line, local, project, and user—to identify which rule is blocking the action and determine whether it should be modified or kept in place.
Grant the engineer full unrestricted shell access to circumvent the blocking rule, removing all tool-pattern safeguards rather than adjusting only the problematic rule.

explanation: Permission denials are diagnostic signals that require methodical investigation, not workarounds or wholesale removal of controls. Option C is correct because it prescribes a systematic examination of all permission scopes to identify the source of the denial and make an informed decision about whether to amend or retain it. Options A and D attempt to bypass the permission system rather than understand it, while Option B eliminates all security controls indiscriminately, creating risk across the entire environment.

question: You are establishing best practices for onboarding Claude Code across a large engineering department. Which two practices should be included in the rollout plan? Each correct answer presents a complete solution. (Select two.)

options.text: Configure team-shared Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and permission rules at the project scope under version control.
Apply organization-level configuration centrally for security-sensitive settings that engineers cannot override individually.
Place security-sensitive permission rules at the local scope so individual engineers can customize them as their work evolves.
Configure team-shared MCP servers at the user scope to ensure all team members have identical access.
Place personal IDE settings at the project scope so they remain consistent across all team members.

explanation: Effective team rollouts require both shared infrastructure under version control and centralized enforcement of security policies. Option A is correct because project scope with version control allows teams to maintain consistent MCP servers and rules while enabling collaboration and auditability. Option B is correct because managed, centralized configuration ensures that security-critical settings cannot be weakened by individual engineers, reducing risk across the organization. Options C and D invert the correct scopes—local scope is for personal customization, not security rules, and user scope is for individual settings, not team infrastructure. Option E misuses project scope for personal preferences rather than team-shared resources.

question: You are defining the scope of a technical guide for a delivery team that will construct and deploy a new system. What should the guide include to best support their work?

options.text: Module responsibilities, interfaces and contracts between modules, call flows for key scenarios, tunable parameters with default values, and operational procedures for running the system.
Module responsibilities and interface contracts alone, omitting call flows, parameter specifications, default values, and operational procedures.
A high-level architecture summary and call flows for key scenarios, but excluding interface contracts, parameter details, and operational procedures.
A high-level architecture overview and a catalog of known constraints, without module diagrams, interface specifications, parameter tables, or operational procedures.

explanation: Delivery teams need comprehensive, actionable guidance that covers both design and operations. Option A is correct because it provides the complete set of information required to implement and run the system: component responsibilities clarify ownership, contracts ensure correct integration, flow diagrams show how components interact, parameters enable configuration, and runbooks prepare the team for operational tasks. Options B, C, and D each omit critical categories—B lacks operational guidance, C omits contracts and configuration details, and D provides only overview-level information without implementation or operational specifics.

question: You are establishing monitoring for a Claude-powered application and must complete planning activities before deploying instrumentation. Which two activities must be finished BEFORE deploying metrics and trace collection? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. (Select two.)

options.text: Identify the metrics and the data dimensions the application will track across typical and stress-test scenarios.
Calibrate alert thresholds using baseline measurements from normal operation to minimize unnecessary alerts.
Establish the service-level objectives (SLOs) and the failure budgets the application will be accountable to.
Construct the visualization dashboards that display metrics and dimensions at the frequency the team requires.
Write documentation for the dashboards, alert rules, and incident-response procedures for the on-call team.

explanation: Pre-instrumentation planning must define what you will measure and what success looks like; post-instrumentation work uses the data to refine thresholds and build tools. Option A is correct because you must decide which metrics and dimensions matter before you begin collecting data, ensuring you capture relevant signals from the start. Option C is correct because SLOs and error budgets define the targets and acceptable failure rates before instrumentation, allowing you to design metrics that measure progress toward those goals. Options B, D, and E are post-instrumentation activities that depend on having baseline data: thresholds are tuned after observing normal behavior, dashboards are built once you have data to display, and documentation is written after you understand what the system produces.

question: Your organization is deploying a Claude-powered customer support system and is concerned about performance degradation in response accuracy following a model update. Which approach most effectively identifies this specific risk before production impact?

options.text: Eliminate systematic testing during model transitions to reduce overhead, relying instead on customer feedback tickets to identify any accuracy issues once the new model is live.
Shuffle evaluation test cases between each model version to ensure fresh assessment conditions and prevent test-set bias.
Defer comprehensive testing until after the upgraded model has already been deployed to production traffic, then monitor for emerging problems.
Preserve a consistent evaluation benchmark with model-specific result tracking so each version is tested against identical criteria prior to deployment.

explanation: Option D is correct because maintaining a stable, version-tracked evaluation set allows direct comparison of model behavior across upgrades and catches performance regressions before they reach users. Options A and C both defer detection until production harm occurs, defeating early risk identification. Option B introduces variability that prevents meaningful version-to-version comparison and masks true drift.

question: After upgrading to a newer Claude version, your RAG pipeline began returning assertions that exceed what the source documents actually contain. What is the most direct way to prevent this specific failure?

options.text: Filter output to only include information directly traceable to sources, enforce citation requirements, and insert a validation layer to confirm alignment.
Establish a fixed benchmark set of adversarial prompts and track scores across model versions.
Implement role-based access control using individual API credentials instead of shared keys to limit document retrieval scope.
Apply content-filtering classifiers to all incoming documents to mark suspicious or untrusted data at ingestion.

explanation: Option A directly addresses hallucination in grounded contexts by constraining the model to source material, requiring attribution, and validating consistency—the core mitigations for this failure mode. Option B measures drift but doesn't prevent unsupported claims. Option C controls access but doesn't address output accuracy. Option D filters inputs rather than outputs, missing the root cause of unsupported assertions in the response.

question: You are conducting a threat modeling exercise for a Claude-integrated system and need to establish the foundation before evaluating potential attacks. Which two prerequisites must be established first to enable meaningful threat assessment? (Select two.)

options.text: Finalize the risk register with identified risks, proposed controls, and residual risk owners assigned.
Propose and prioritize mitigations for each identified threat and designate accountability for residual risk.
Catalog the data, systems, and business functions the deployment will access and classify their sensitivity levels.
Develop mitigation strategies and secure stakeholder approval for accepting remaining risks.
List the adversaries, their capabilities, and the attack methods applicable to this deployment context.

explanation: Options C and E are correct because threat assessment requires knowing what you're protecting (assets and their value) and who/what you're protecting against (threat actors and vectors) before you can evaluate likelihood and impact. Options A, B, and D are downstream activities that depend on threat analysis being complete; they represent mitigation and acceptance rather than the foundational inventory steps.

question: Your architecture team is deciding between Model Context Protocol (MCP), native API calls, and agent delegation for connecting Claude to external services. Which two considerations should guide this decision? (Select two.)

options.text: The availability and comprehensiveness of API documentation provided by each integration option vendor.
Whether your team has hands-on experience deploying any of these integration patterns in prior projects.
Whether the communication channel between services supports TLS or equivalent encryption mechanisms.
Whether the solution must work interchangeably with multiple AI platforms and client types in your ecosystem.
Whether the interaction pattern is request-response and time-critical or involves state management and extended duration.

explanation: Options D and E are correct because they address fundamental architectural trade-offs: portability across the AI ecosystem (D) and interaction characteristics that determine which pattern fits best (E). Option A conflates documentation quality with architectural fit. Option B reflects team experience but shouldn't drive architecture selection. Option C is a baseline security requirement for all three options, not a differentiator.

question: You are planning to embed Claude Code into your team's development workflow and must complete setup work before launching a pilot with early adopters. Which two activities must be finished BEFORE the pilot phase begins? (Select two.)

options.text: Create comprehensive documentation describing the new workflow, decision points, escalation paths, and incident response procedures.
Map which workflow stages benefit from AI assistance and which require final human judgment and control.
Conduct formal change management reviews with all stakeholder teams and secure written approval from leadership.
Refine the workflow based on pilot feedback and prepare for organization-wide rollout.
Set up environment-specific MCP servers, configure access policies, establish agent boundaries, and load persistent project state.

explanation: Options B and E are correct because they represent essential design and technical configuration that must be complete before any pilot can function: identifying where AI adds value and where humans stay in control (B), and provisioning the actual technical infrastructure and permissions (E). Option A is documentation that follows piloting. Option C involves change management timing that may occur in parallel with or after pilot planning. Option D is explicitly a post-pilot activity.

question: You are designing a multi-tenant Claude-powered document-analysis system where marketing teams and legal teams must never access each other's confidential materials. At which point in the processing pipeline should access restrictions be implemented to ensure proper isolation?

options.text: Embed access rules directly into the system prompt as guidelines that Claude will voluntarily respect when filtering its own outputs.
Enforce restrictions at the data-fetching layer, preventing unauthorized materials from being included in the prompt before model processing occurs.
Omit explicit access controls and depend on the model's inherent safety mechanisms to decline requests for restricted information.
Apply filtering only after Claude generates its response, removing sensitive content from the final output.

explanation: Access control must be enforced at the retrieval layer before restricted data ever reaches the model, ensuring that unauthorized information cannot influence the response regardless of the model's behavior. Relying on the system prompt (A) is insufficient because Claude may still reference or reason about materials in the context. Post-response filtering (D) is too late—sensitive data has already been processed. Depending solely on model refusal (C) leaves the system vulnerable to prompt injection or model inconsistencies. Only enforcing controls at the data-fetching stage (B) provides defense-in-depth and prevents unauthorized access from the start.

question: A team is preparing to deploy a Claude-based resume-ranking tool for hiring decisions. A manager claims that because Claude was not trained on the organization's hiring history, a comprehensive bias assessment is unnecessary. Which two statements most effectively counter this argument? (Select two.)

options.text: Simply disclosing that an AI system is used satisfies all fairness and transparency requirements without additional testing.
Bias assessment is only mandatory when the underlying training data explicitly includes demographic information.
Pretraining introduces latent demographic patterns that can produce unfair outcomes in hiring contexts even without organization-specific fine-tuning.
The tool should be validated using metrics that measure performance disparities across demographic groups before launch.
A published responsible-use guide from the model vendor eliminates the need for independent bias evaluation.

explanation: Claude's pretraining data contains demographic patterns that can manifest as disparate impact in hiring, making bias evaluation essential regardless of whether organization-specific fine-tuning occurred (C). Outcome-disparity testing across protected groups is a standard best practice for high-stakes hiring systems and must be conducted before deployment (D). Transparency alone (A) and vendor guidance (E) do not substitute for empirical evaluation. Bias assessment is not limited to datasets with explicit demographic labels (B); implicit associations in language models can produce biased outcomes.

question: A product team is executing a Claude deployment with a fixed timeline when a key stakeholder requests a substantial addition to the feature set. How should you respond to balance the stakeholder's needs with realistic delivery constraints?

options.text: Shield the delivery team from the request to prevent scheduling friction, allowing the addition to proceed without their knowledge of the timeline pressure.
Immediately reject the request without exploring what problem the stakeholder is trying to solve or discussing feasible alternatives.
Validate the stakeholder's underlying goal, clearly articulate the trade-offs involved (deferral, scope reduction, or schedule extension), and let the stakeholder decide how to proceed.
Approve the additional scope without communicating the schedule or resource implications, allowing constraints to become apparent only when delays occur.

explanation: Transparent communication about scope trade-offs (C) respects both the stakeholder's needs and the team's capacity. Hiding requests (A) and proceeding without acknowledgment (D) erode trust and create schedule crises. Outright rejection (B) dismisses legitimate stakeholder concerns and misses opportunities to find creative solutions. The best approach validates the underlying need while presenting concrete options, enabling informed decision-making at the leadership level.

question: A Claude-based legal-research assistant has begun generating responses that contradict the documents it retrieves, even though the retrieval system has not been modified. Which two investigative steps will most quickly pinpoint what has changed? (Select two.)

options.text: Expand the context window to allow the model to ingest more retrieved document excerpts per query.
Upgrade the embedding model used by the retrieval index to improve relevance ranking.
Test whether the contradiction behavior occurs when using the previous Claude model version to isolate whether a model change is responsible.
Lower the temperature parameter to reduce the randomness in model outputs.
Review the system prompt to verify that citation and grounding instructions are still in place and unchanged.

explanation: Testing against the prior model version (C) directly isolates whether a model update introduced the regression. Reviewing the system prompt (E) determines whether grounding instructions were accidentally removed or weakened, which would cause citation failures. Expanding context (A) and upgrading embeddings (B) do not diagnose root cause—they are optimization steps. Lowering temperature (D) may reduce variance but does not identify why the model is contradicting sources in the first place.

question: Your organization plans to roll out Claude Skills across 280 engineers in 12 teams, with Skills encoding deployment procedures, testing protocols, and runbook templates. Leadership wants to ensure Skills remain reliable and current without creating a bottleneck at a central approval stage. What governance structure should you propose?

options.text: Allow any of the 280 engineers to author and publish Skills independently without coordination.
Assign all Skill creation and maintenance to a single central platform team.
Enable each of the 12 teams to author and publish Skills with no review process.
Distribute Skill authorship across the 12 teams while maintaining a centralized approval and release workflow.

explanation: Federated authorship (D) balances ownership and domain expertise at the team level with centralized quality gates, preventing both bottlenecks and unchecked drift. Individual authorship (A) leads to inconsistency and quality loss. Centralized authorship (B) becomes a bottleneck as the organization scales. Fully decentralized publishing (C) removes accountability and allows outdated or incorrect Skills to proliferate. The federated model ensures teams maintain their own standards while a central gate preserves organizational consistency.

question: Your team is building a customer support automation system that must decide when to route inquiries to human agents. What approach to defining routing criteria will ensure the most reliable and predictable handoff decisions?

options.text: Allow the model to make independent escalation decisions on each request based on its own judgment, with no predefined confidence levels or decision categories.
Escalate only after a customer has already experienced a problem and filed a formal complaint, once the automated system has already processed the request.
Escalate based on whoever is on duty and has available time, using informal guidelines that vary depending on team circumstances.

Escalate when confidence scores fall below a specified threshold, when the issue affects critical business functions, when content classifiers flag ambiguity, or when the customer explicitly requests human review.

explanation: Option D establishes objective, measurable criteria—confidence thresholds, impact classification, classifier-based signals, and explicit customer requests—that enable consistent, reproducible escalation decisions. Options A and C rely on subjective judgment or availability, leading to inconsistent outcomes. Option B escalates too late, after the automated system has already made a potentially incorrect decision without human oversight.

question: Your team is designing a system that integrates Claude with internal APIs and databases. During a security review, you identify two issues that represent genuine vulnerabilities. Which two findings are valid security concerns? (Select two.)

options.text: API calls execute on the backend using a service account with permissions limited to the specific requested operation.
Database passwords and API keys are embedded directly in the prompt text, creating exposure through system logs and distributed traces.
Access controls are applied only at the final response layer after the model has already retrieved sensitive data from the backend.
User-specific access tokens are obtained via OAuth, scoped to minimal required permissions, and refreshed during the session.
All data transferred between the client and backend is protected using TLS encryption.

explanation: Options B and C are genuine security gaps. Option B exposes credentials in logs and traces where they can be intercepted or logged. Option C applies access controls too late—the model retrieves restricted data before authorization is checked, violating the principle of enforcing controls at the point of access. Options A, D, and E represent security best practices: least-privilege service accounts, OAuth with scope restrictions, and transport-layer encryption all reduce risk.

question: Your organization is adopting Claude Code for technical review tasks in your development workflow. Leadership wants AI-assisted analysis while preserving the existing requirement that a human team member must approve all code changes before merging. Which implementation approach aligns with this requirement?

options.text: Claude Code analyzes the code and posts findings as a review comment, while the human reviewer maintains full control over the approval and merge decision through existing branch protections.
Claude Code automatically merges all reviewed code, removing the human approval step to accelerate the workflow.
Claude Code modifies the branch protection settings to eliminate the human approval requirement, streamlining the merge process.
Claude Code removes low-quality code changes from the repository without notifying the author or leaving any record.

explanation: Option A implements AI-assisted review as an input to human decision-making while preserving human control over the approval gate. This satisfies the requirement for AI assistance without removing the mandatory human review. Options B and C both eliminate human approval, violating the stated requirement. Option D removes human oversight entirely and lacks transparency, creating governance and accountability problems.

question: Your team is deciding how to package a new feature that generates standardized compliance documents from internal data. The feature uses a fixed procedural template with built-in examples, does not require real-time external data, and must work across three environments: claude.ai, a company API, and Claude Code. Which consideration most strongly supports implementing this as a Skill?

options.text: The feature needs to fetch live data from external regulatory databases.
The feature must be invoked from a developer's local terminal.
The feature requires authentication through the corporate identity system.
The feature is based on procedural knowledge and requires no live external-system integration.

explanation: Option D is the strongest factor favoring a Skill implementation. Skills excel at packaging procedural knowledge, fixed templates, and examples in a portable format that works consistently across claude.ai, APIs, and Claude Code without external dependencies. Options A and C describe scenarios where an MCP server would be more appropriate due to the need for live system integration and authentication. Option B is neutral—both Skills and MCP servers can be CLI-callable depending on the integration approach.

question: A platform team managing a high-traffic Claude pipeline needs to reduce both per-request costs and response latency while maintaining output quality for their primary use cases. Which two optimizations will improve both metrics at the same time? (Select two.)

options.text: Implement prompt caching to reduce the number of billable input tokens when the same system prompt is used repeatedly.
Direct routine queries to a smaller, more efficient model variant and reserve the larger model for queries that require advanced reasoning.
Increase the max_tokens parameter to prevent response truncation and reduce the need for follow-up requests.
Fetch the entire source dataset into the context window before generation begins.
Expand the system prompt with additional in-context examples on every request.

explanation: Options A and B both reduce cost and latency simultaneously. Prompt caching decreases billable tokens and reduces processing overhead on repeated requests. Model routing avoids the computational cost and latency of the larger model for simple queries. Options C, D, and E all increase input tokens or processing requirements: increasing max_tokens increases cost, fetching full datasets inflates context size, and adding examples on every request increases token usage and latency.

question: Your organization manages a critical customer-facing disclosure statement that must be consistently applied across support interactions, account provisioning, and marketing communications. The disclosure requirements are updated by legal counsel approximately three to five times annually. You need to establish a reusable approach so that Claude enforces this disclosure across all three channels without duplication or inconsistency. Which two architectural choices should you implement? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. (Select two.)

options.text: Develop the disclosure as a Claude Skill maintained and versioned by the legal team.
Copy the disclosure language directly into the system prompt configuration for each channel at deployment time.
Maintain the disclosure in a centralized knowledge base that all three channels query at runtime.
Ask each channel's product team to independently adapt and rewrite the disclosure for their specific use case.
Invoke the same Claude Skill across all three channel implementations.

explanation: A and E together form the correct solution: packaging the disclosure as a Skill (A) gives the legal team direct ownership and simplifies updates, while referencing that Skill from all channels (E) ensures consistency without duplication. Option B embeds the text directly, making updates difficult and creating drift. Option C uses a retrieval corpus, which adds latency and complexity compared to Skill-based composition. Option D introduces inconsistency by allowing independent rewrites, defeating the purpose of a single source of truth.

question: You are troubleshooting an MCP integration that works reliably after the initial setup but encounters errors during the first execution. The system displayed several authorization prompts when the integration was first activated. What is the most appropriate diagnostic and resolution approach?

options.text: Identify the initial authorization grant as the likely root cause, document this expected first-run behavior in setup documentation, and verify that subsequent executions function correctly.
Perform a complete system reset to eliminate all cached permissions before investigating whether the authorization process was responsible.
Suppress all system authorization dialogs at the operating-system level, accept the security trade-offs, and move forward without re-testing the failure scenario.
Classify the first-run failure as a persistent defect, retire the MCP integration, and deploy an alternative without confirming whether subsequent runs succeed.

explanation: Option A is correct because it follows a methodical troubleshooting approach: recognize the authorization process as the likely cause, document the expected behavior, and confirm the fix works. Option B is premature and destructive—resetting the system before confirming the root cause wastes time and may destroy useful diagnostic information. Option C introduces security risk by disabling authorization mechanisms without justification. Option D abandons the integration prematurely without validating whether the issue is actually permanent.

question: You are evaluating potential security threats in a Claude-powered application that integrates both document-retrieval capabilities and the ability to make outbound API requests to external services. Which situation most clearly represents a data-exfiltration vulnerability?

options.text: The external API endpoint responds with HTTP 200 when the assistant makes a legitimate request to a whitelisted service in response to a user's data-inquiry request.
The user asks a straightforward question and the assistant provides a straightforward response.
A retrieved document contains instructions that manipulate the model into invoking the outbound API tool to transmit confidential information to an unauthorized external server.
The document-retrieval tool returns information that the requesting user has legitimate access rights to view.

explanation: Option C is correct because it describes a direct attack vector: adversarial content in a document can hijack the model's reasoning to exfiltrate sensitive data to attacker-controlled endpoints. Option A shows normal, authorized behavior with appropriate allowlisting. Option B represents benign interaction with no security concern. Option D shows proper access control functioning as designed. Only Option C demonstrates an actual compromise of the system's intended data-handling boundaries.

question: A development organization is rolling out Claude Code across 150 engineering staff. A senior developer suggests that AI-generated code changes below 30 lines should skip the standard peer-review process to reduce review bottlenecks and accelerate delivery. Which two concerns aligned with quality-assurance principles should you raise? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. (Select two.)

options.text: Bypassing review removes a critical validation step that confirms the correctness and safety of AI-generated code throughout the development pipeline.
The team should hire additional reviewers to handle the review volume rather than exempting any changes from scrutiny.
The line-count threshold is an unreliable indicator of actual risk, since a small change can introduce critical vulnerabilities or architectural problems.
All AI-generated code should be rejected automatically as a matter of policy.
Lines of code is a poor metric for assessing the true risk profile of a change.

explanation: Option A correctly identifies that peer review is a critical quality gate for validating AI-generated code, regardless of its source. Option C directly addresses the flawed premise of using line count as a risk metric—small changes can introduce severe security vulnerabilities, logic errors, or architectural issues that require human review. Option E, while technically true that lines of code is a poor risk metric, is essentially a restatement of C but less specific to the quality-assurance context of the question. Option B suggests an impractical solution that doesn't address the core quality concern, and Option D represents an extreme policy that contradicts the premise of adopting Claude Code.

question: A technology director at Acme Corp is evaluating two competing approaches to integrate Claude into the developer experience. Option 1 embeds Claude Code directly within the code editor for real-time generation and inline feedback. Option 2 centralizes all code-generation requests through a team communication platform without editor integration. Which two assessments most accurately reflect how these options align with productivity and usability goals? (Select two.)

options.text: Option 2 is preferable because routing requests through the communication platform creates a searchable history of all code-generation interactions.
Option 2 imposes additional friction by forcing developers to switch tools and contexts away from their primary development environment, reducing overall efficiency.
Option 1 minimizes context switching by delivering AI capabilities at the point where developers are actively writing code, enhancing productivity.
Option 2 accelerates development velocity because asynchronous notifications through the communication platform allow parallel work queuing.
Both approaches deliver equivalent outcomes because the underlying model and code-generation quality are the same regardless of how the tool is accessed.

explanation: Options B and C are correct: B explains that Option 2 introduces workflow friction by requiring developers to leave their IDE, which undermines productivity goals. C explains that Option 1 reduces context switching by keeping assistance available where developers work, directly supporting efficiency objectives. Option A focuses on auditability rather than productivity. Option D confuses asynchronicity with velocity—a communication platform doesn't inherently speed up development. Option E incorrectly assumes that integration point is irrelevant; user experience and workflow integration significantly impact adoption and actual productivity gains.

question: You are developing a technical reference document for deploying a multi-component system and need to establish a clear plan before beginning to write. Which two preparatory activities should you complete BEFORE starting to draft the content sections? Each correct answer represents a key planning step. (Select two.)

options.text: Define who will use the document and clarify what specific problems or decisions each audience segment needs to resolve.
Secure budget approval and resource allocation for the full implementation project timeline.
Conduct a pilot deployment with early adopters to gather feedback before finalizing the written guide.
Create a governance structure including ownership, review schedules, and sign-off authorities in a version-controlled repository.
Develop a structural blueprint detailing key sections such as executive summary, system components, interface specifications, operational workflows, troubleshooting procedures, and known constraints.

explanation: Before drafting any section of a technical guide, you must first understand your audience and their information needs (A), and create a structural outline that maps what each section will cover (E). These upstream planning activities prevent rework and ensure the guide stays focused. Option B (budget) is a business concern unrelated to documentation planning. Option C (pilot deployment) is a validation activity that happens after drafting, not before. Option D (governance setup) is important for ongoing maintenance but not a prerequisite to starting the draft itself.

question: You are implementing a content moderation workflow for a high-volume customer-support chatbot where manual review of every response is not practical. Which approach to sampling best achieves both operational efficiency and meaningful quality assurance?

options.text: Skip all manual review and depend on user feedback mechanisms to surface problems only after they have already reached customers.
Prioritize review of outputs with low confidence scores and high business impact, supplemented by a representative random sample of routine, high-confidence outputs.
Review only outputs with high confidence and low risk, while systematically excluding low-confidence and high-impact cases from review.
Implement mandatory human review for every single output before it reaches any user.

explanation: Risk-stratified sampling (B) is the industry standard for high-volume systems because it concentrates limited review effort on the outputs most likely to cause harm or reveal systemic issues, while still maintaining statistical visibility into routine performance. Option A abandons oversight entirely and creates liability. Option C inverts the logic and ignores the cases most likely to fail. Option D is operationally infeasible at scale and wastes resources on low-risk outputs that need less scrutiny.

question: Your team deployed an updated prompt configuration, and a suite of previously stable test cases now produces different results than expected. Which category of test is explicitly designed to catch this type of regression?

options.text: End-to-end tests that verify all system components work together correctly after deployment.
Security tests that attempt to manipulate inputs or bypass system safeguards through malicious techniques.
Baseline tests that compare current outputs against a frozen set of previously validated reference outputs.
Smoke tests that quickly verify that critical functionality is operational after a change.

explanation: Regression tests (C) are specifically designed to detect when changes to code or configuration cause previously working behavior to break by comparing current outputs against a stable baseline of known-good results. Option A (end-to-end) tests system integration but doesn't focus on detecting changes in established behavior. Option B (security tests) target vulnerabilities, not functional regressions. Option D (smoke tests) verify basic operability but lack the detailed comparison needed to spot subtle output changes.

question: You are building a comprehensive test plan for a Claude-powered financial data analysis tool that processes confidential information. Which two test categories should you emphasize to ensure the system is both resilient to deliberate attacks and functionally correct across all connected components? (Select two.)

options.text: Adversarial tests using injection attacks, malformed payloads, and attempts to circumvent safety mechanisms.
Baseline tests comparing outputs against a stable reference set of historical correct results.
Rapid-check tests that validate basic system responsiveness and availability after each code update.
Full-stack tests that trace requests through all system layers and verify correct behavior at integration points.
Isolated tests targeting only the prompt-template rendering and formatting logic in isolation.

explanation: For a sensitive financial system, you must prioritize adversarial testing (A) to validate that the system resists attacks and maintains safety boundaries, and integration testing (D) to ensure that all components work together correctly end-to-end, because failures at integration points can expose data or cause incorrect analysis. Option B (baseline tests) is useful but less critical than the two chosen. Option C (rapid checks) provides only shallow coverage. Option E (unit tests) are too narrow and miss cross-component issues where sensitive data could be mishandled.

question: A security team is documenting potential failure modes in a Claude-powered question-answering system that retrieves and reasons over internal documents. Which two risks are characteristic of language-model-based systems and cannot be attributed to general software infrastructure problems? (Select two.)

options.text: A revoked security certificate prevents the service from establishing encrypted connections to external APIs.
A network outage in the data retrieval layer returns an empty or incomplete document set to the model.
The model declines a valid user question because overly sensitive safety rules are triggered by benign keywords or patterns.
Incorrect routing configuration at the load balancer directs traffic to an obsolete service endpoint.
The model generates a confident, detailed answer that sounds reasonable but is not actually supported by any of the retrieved source documents.

explanation: Options C and E represent failure modes intrinsic to large language models: C describes overfitting to surface-level safety heuristics (false refusals), and E describes hallucination (generating plausible but unsupported content). These are LLM-specific behaviors. Options A (certificate management), B (data retrieval infrastructure), and D (load balancing) are generic software and infrastructure issues that could occur in any system regardless of whether it uses AI.

question: A development team has deployed an AI-powered contract-analysis tool that now processes documents in 8 minutes instead of the previous 52 minutes. Analysts report reduced time spent on initial review, yet the total number of contracts completed per month remains unchanged. The system's error-handling mechanisms have triggered additional API calls, raising cloud expenses by 19%. Furthermore, legal reviewers must spend an average of 7 minutes validating and correcting the tool's analysis on each contract. How should these findings be categorized across business-value dimensions?

options.text: Findings 1 and 2 represent efficiency improvements; Finding 3 reflects infrastructure cost growth; Finding 4 represents a quality-assurance burden.
Finding 1 demonstrates a transformation breakthrough; Finding 2 shows efficiency gain; Finding 3 indicates performance degradation; Finding 4 represents a cost factor.
Findings 1 and 4 combined show net performance improvement; Finding 2 reveals an unrealized productivity opportunity; Finding 3 stems from architectural inefficiency.

Finding 1 represents an efficiency gain; Finding 2 indicates that productivity benefits have not materialized; Finding 3 constitutes a solution-cost problem; Finding 4 is an efficiency loss that partially negates Finding 1.

explanation: The correct answer properly distinguishes between efficiency (time reduction), productivity (output volume), cost (infrastructure spend), and net value (gains minus offsetting losses). Option D correctly identifies that while processing time improved (efficiency), the unchanged output volume means productivity hasn't improved, the increased API calls represent a cost issue, and the validation time required partially offsets the initial speed gain. The other options conflate these distinct business-value dimensions or mischaracterize the nature of each observation.

question: A customer-support chatbot demonstrates a 91 percent rate at which users accept the first response without requesting changes. However, post-interaction surveys indicate that users frequently modify the chatbot's suggested solutions after reviewing them more thoroughly. The program manager advocates for immediate production rollout based on the acceptance metric. Which two Discernment-competency concerns should be surfaced BEFORE greenlighting the deployment? (Select two.)

options.text: The acceptance rate alone is sufficient evidence that the system is ready for enterprise deployment.
The survey sample size may not adequately represent the diversity of all customer segments.
The unaddressed decision factors represent a gap in the system's input requirements.
Acceptance metrics do not confirm whether recommendations remain valid after user modification.
The pilot timeframe was likely insufficient to assess performance consistency over multiple seasons.

explanation: Option D correctly identifies that acceptance metrics (users not requesting immediate changes) don't validate whether the solutions actually work after users modify them—this is a critical discernment gap between surface-level acceptance and actual solution quality. Option B appropriately raises concern about whether the survey sample adequately represents all customer segments, which is essential for responsible deployment decisions. Option C mischaracterizes the issue as missing "input requirements" when the problem is actually about measurement validity and post-acceptance outcomes. Option E introduces an unsupported assumption about seasonal variation that isn't indicated by the scenario. Option A is clearly incorrect as it contradicts the premise of identifying concerns.

question: You are designing a governance framework for AI-assisted decision-making in hiring processes. Which two items should be included in the ethics-review protocol? Each correct answer provides a necessary control. (Select two.)

options.text: Ensure that the licensing agreement with the AI provider permits use in employment contexts.
Validate that recommendations do not depend on statistical assumptions about candidate groups that the training data cannot substantiate.
Establish that consequential hiring decisions remain subject to human judgment and accountability rather than being delegated entirely to the AI system.
Limit ethics review to recommendations with confidence scores above a specified threshold.
Verify that response times and throughput meet organizational SLA targets across all candidate populations.

explanation: Options B and C address core ethical concerns: B prevents discriminatory generalization by ensuring recommendations are grounded in defensible data patterns, while C preserves human accountability for high-stakes decisions rather than outsourcing responsibility to the model. Option A addresses licensing but not ethics. Option D is counterproductive—low-confidence recommendations may pose greater ethical risk and require closer review. Option E addresses performance SLAs, not ethics.

question: A colleague is finalizing a system prompt that includes conflicting directives: one section instructs the model to decline requests requiring information not in the provided context, while another section encourages the model to provide helpful elaboration on related topics. Which approach best resolves this issue?

options.text: Insert a meta-instruction that directs the model to weigh both instructions and apply the one that seems most fitting for each individual query.
Revise or eliminate the elaboration instruction so the prompt maintains consistent boundaries around context-supported responses only.
Increase temperature settings to introduce sufficient output variation that the contradiction becomes less noticeable.
Retain both instructions and allow the model's internal reasoning to determine which instruction takes precedence on each occasion.

explanation: Option B is correct because contradictory instructions create unpredictable behavior and undermine prompt reliability. The proper fix is to align the instructions so they reinforce a single, clear behavioral boundary. Option A is ineffective—adding a meta-instruction about instruction selection doesn't resolve the underlying contradiction. Option C masks the problem rather than solving it and introduces uncontrolled variability. Option D assumes the model will reliably resolve ambiguity, which is neither guaranteed nor appropriate for critical deployments.

question: You are assessing whether a Claude-powered system complies with a particular data-protection regulation. Which two actions must be completed BEFORE beginning to map the system's data flows against specific regulatory requirements? Each correct answer represents a necessary prerequisite. (Select two.)

options.text: Analyze the existing control environment against regulatory mandates to pinpoint areas of non-compliance.
Determine which aspects of the regulation apply based on the nature of the data, geographic scope, and user base.
Coordinate with engineering leadership to establish a timeline and resource plan for addressing identified gaps.
Prepare a formal assessment documenting gaps, proposed solutions, residual risks, and stakeholder approval.
Catalog the compliance capabilities offered by the vendor and verify which ones are currently operational.

explanation: Options B and E must precede the mapping phase: B ensures you understand which regulatory rules actually apply to this specific system (applicability scoping), and E inventories the compliance tools already available before you identify gaps. Option A (gap analysis) comes after mapping. Options C and D are downstream remediation and documentation steps that follow gap identification, not prerequisites to it.

question: Your team is building a machine learning pipeline that relies on Claude for feature engineering. Currently, every pipeline run requires engineers to manually provide detailed instructions about the feature schema, validation rules, and naming conventions to Claude. This repetition is slowing down iteration. What is the most effective way to eliminate this recurring overhead?

options.text: Discontinue using Claude for feature engineering tasks to avoid the need to provide context at the start of each pipeline run, accepting reduced automation capabilities.
Store the feature schema, validation rules, and naming conventions in a version-controlled configuration file that the pipeline loads and passes to Claude automatically on each run.
Have engineers optimize their manual explanations of the feature requirements to be more concise, reducing the time spent without changing the fundamental repetitive process.
Remove all documented feature specifications and validation rules so there is no context to provide to Claude at pipeline start, accepting degraded data quality and inconsistency.

explanation: Option B directly addresses the inefficiency by persisting context in a reusable artifact that eliminates manual re-explanation. Option A abandons the tool entirely, losing productivity. Option C merely reduces symptoms without solving the underlying problem of repeated manual work. Option D eliminates the problem by removing standards, which creates new problems rather than solving the original one.

question: Your organization runs a custom-built claims processing system on cloud infrastructure that uses five coordinated microservices to handle policy validation, adjudication, payment authorization, audit logging, and notification delivery. Your platform team currently dedicates 35 percent of engineering time to managing service orchestration, database synchronization, and failure recovery. The CTO wants to evaluate whether a managed claims platform could free up engineering resources. Your compliance officer mandates that all policyholder personally identifiable information remain within your organization's private data center. What should be the primary consideration in your evaluation?

options.text: Whether the managed platform's microservice architecture matches your current five-service decomposition.
Whether the managed platform reduces the average cost per claim processed across your current volume.
Whether the managed platform uses the same message queue technology your team currently uses for inter-service communication.
Whether the managed platform's data residency and storage mechanisms comply with your private data center requirement.

explanation: Option D is the gating constraint—if the managed platform cannot meet the compliance requirement for data location, no other benefit matters. Options A, B, and C address optimization or compatibility concerns, but they are secondary to the mandatory compliance requirement. A solution that reduces costs or engineering overhead but violates data residency mandates is not viable.

question: Your organization provides contract review services where paralegals analyze complex commercial agreements averaging 120,000 tokens each. Each contract is reviewed by paralegals an average of 18 times as terms are negotiated. Your current system re-sends the entire contract text with each review request. The CFO wants to lower the operational cost per review cycle while maintaining accuracy. Your legal compliance team requires that contract data remain within your secure internal environment. Which strategy best meets these constraints?

options.text: Generate a condensed summary of each contract at the first review and use that summary for all subsequent review requests.
Use prompt caching to store the full contract text once and reuse it across the 18 review queries without re-transmission.
Embed contracts into a semantic search index and retrieve only the top matching sections for each review query.
Switch to a smaller, faster Claude model variant to reduce the per-token cost of each review request.

explanation: Option B leverages prompt caching to avoid re-transmitting the contract while preserving full context and accuracy, directly reducing costs per query. Option A loses detail and context by summarizing, which risks accuracy. Option C requires external storage, which violates the internal-environment requirement. Option D reduces capability and may harm review quality without addressing the core inefficiency of re-transmission.

question: You are designing a content moderation system for user-generated submissions that follows a consistent sequence: validate format, detect policy violations, assign severity level, and write results to a compliance database. Which architectural pattern is most appropriate for this use case and why?

options.text: An agentic pattern, because only agents can invoke tools to write results to the database and therefore only agents can complete the final persistence step.
An agentic pattern, because agents' flexible reasoning produces more reliable severity classifications than deterministic workflows.
An agentic pattern, because agents are universally superior to workflows and should be used for all production systems regardless of task structure.
A workflow pattern, because the steps are sequential and deterministic, and predictable token consumption is preferable to the variability introduced by agent reasoning.

explanation: Option D is correct because the moderation process has fixed, well-defined steps in a known sequence with no branching or decision-making required. Workflows excel at this use case and provide cost predictability. Option A is factually wrong—both workflows and agents support tool invocation. Option B mischaracterizes the task as needing flexible reasoning when it requires consistent rule application. Option C overstates agent capabilities and ignores the importance of matching the pattern to the problem structure.

question: You are documenting operational procedures for a production Claude-powered customer support system. What should the runbook contain to enable the on-call team to respond effectively to incidents?

options.text: System metrics and log locations only, without guidance on recognizing problems, investigating root causes, fixing issues, or notifying management.

Descriptions of typical failure modes and how to diagnose them, steps to resolve or mitigate each issue, who to contact if the problem persists, procedures to restore service, and pointers to relevant monitoring dashboards.
Instructions for recognizing alerts and troubleshooting steps only, without escalation contacts, recovery procedures, or references to monitoring tools.
Escalation contacts and service recovery procedures only, without guidance on recognizing problems, diagnosing root causes, or accessing monitoring information.

explanation: Option B provides comprehensive incident response coverage: it enables the on-call engineer to recognize issues, understand them, fix them, escalate if needed, and restore service. Options A, C, and D each omit critical components—A lacks actionable guidance, C lacks escalation and recovery, and D lacks problem recognition and diagnosis. A complete runbook must support the full incident lifecycle.

question: Your team is establishing performance guarantees for a Claude-powered content moderation system. Which approach to defining these guarantees will be most useful for operational management and accountability?

options.text: A commitment that the system will be 'highly accurate and dependable,' without specifying which metric, numerical target, or assessment period applies.
A quantified commitment such as 'false-negative rate below 2% measured over a rolling 30-day period, with automatic escalation to the security team if the threshold is exceeded.'
A target based on user feedback statements like 'stakeholders report confidence in the system,' which cannot be objectively tracked or used to initiate a formal response plan.
A commitment that identifies the metric and target percentage but does not specify the measurement interval or what happens when the target is missed.

explanation: Option B is correct because it specifies a concrete metric (false-negative rate), a clear threshold (2%), a defined measurement window (30-day rolling period), and a defined consequence (escalation). This structure enables teams to monitor performance objectively and respond systematically to breaches. Options A and C lack measurable criteria and actionable triggers. Option D omits critical details (measurement window and consequence) that prevent consistent compliance assessment and remediation.

question: Your development team is deciding whether to build a dedicated agent for automated API contract validation or continue using Claude's general-purpose capabilities for this work. What condition most strongly supports creating a specialized agent?

options.text: The team performs API contract validation regularly across multiple projects, requires a tailored system prompt that enforces validation rules, needs restricted access to specific testing tools, and benefits from a consistent model configuration.
The team has a single, non-repeating request for API validation that will not require a specialized system prompt, restricted tool access, or dedicated model tuning.
The team does not have recurring validation tasks and uses Claude primarily for general exploratory work that does not warrant a specialized system prompt or constrained tool set.
The team prefers to run all Claude interactions with a single generic system prompt and no task-specific customization, tool restrictions, or model selection.

explanation: Option A is correct because a dedicated agent is justified when there is a recurring, specialized task that benefits from a focused system prompt, restricted tool permissions, and intentional model selection—all of which improve consistency and safety over many sessions. Options B and C describe one-time or general work that does not justify the overhead of a dedicated agent. Option D reflects a preference against specialization, which contradicts the conditions under which agents provide value.

question: A logistics company is considering automating shipment-status dispute resolution using Claude, with no human approval required for disputes under $200. The team argues that low-value disputes are inherently safe and that human review would slow down resolution. How should you evaluate this proposal?

options.text: All automated decisions must include human review, regardless of the financial amount or risk profile involved.
The scope of automated decision-making should be determined by the nature and severity of the risk, not by transaction value alone.
Automation scope should be expanded as much as possible to maximize speed and efficiency, with financial thresholds as the primary control.
Automated handling of financial disputes should be avoided in all cases because financial decisions inherently require human judgment.

explanation: Option B is correct because delegation decisions must be grounded in risk assessment—the type of harm, likelihood of error, and downstream consequences—rather than transaction size alone. A low-dollar dispute could still involve reputational damage, customer relationship harm, or systematic errors that affect many customers. Option A is overly rigid and ignores legitimate automation opportunities. Option C prioritizes speed over safety and misapplies financial thresholds as a risk proxy. Option D rejects automation categorically, which is neither practical nor aligned with responsible delegation principles.

question: You are designing a governance structure for a multi-stakeholder review process around a Claude deployment. Which two practices should be embedded in this structure? Each answer represents a standalone best practice.

options.text: Archive video recordings of all review sessions and share them broadly with stakeholders who were unable to participate synchronously.
When stakeholders disagree, refer the disagreement to senior leadership for a final decision without further discussion.
Assign facilitation responsibilities to different stakeholder groups in rotation so that no single group controls the agenda.
Establish a repeating schedule for the review process so that expectations and assumptions can be revisited and adjusted as circumstances change.
Address conflicting stakeholder viewpoints directly and work toward alignment rather than allowing disagreements to remain unresolved.

explanation: Options D and E are correct. Option D ensures the governance structure remains responsive to evolving conditions and does not become static or obsolete. Option E prevents misalignment from festering and ensures all stakeholders' concerns are surfaced and addressed, which builds trust and shared ownership. Option A focuses on asynchronous access rather than active engagement and alignment. Option B suppresses healthy dialogue and concentrates decision-making power. Option C, while promoting shared ownership, is less essential than D and E for establishing effective feedback and alignment.

question: You are auditing telemetry collection across a distributed agent orchestration platform. Which two issues represent genuine observability shortfalls? Each correct answer presents a complete solution. (Select two.)

options.text: Individual agent actions are recorded as distinct trace events and forwarded to a centralized tracing system.
Performance metrics including response time and token consumption are continuously published to a monitoring service.
External service invocations and their results are logged with masking applied to personally identifiable information.
Claude model specification and release version are absent from the metadata attached to each interaction.
Session-level identifiers fail to flow through connections between orchestrator components and downstream services.

explanation: Options D and E identify genuine observability gaps that would impair system monitoring and debugging. D represents missing critical metadata needed to track model behavior changes across versions, while E indicates a failure in distributed tracing fundamentals—correlation IDs are essential for following requests through multi-component systems. Options A, B, and C describe proper observability practices already in place, so they are not gaps.

question: You are selecting a model for a spam detection pipeline that must process thousands of messages daily with strict millisecond-level latency constraints and uses straightforward categorical labels. Which choice best matches this deployment profile?

options.text: Opus, because comprehensive analytical reasoning ensures spam patterns are identified with maximum precision in all scenarios.
Haiku, because its speed and cost efficiency suit high-throughput classification tasks with minimal reasoning overhead.
Sonnet, because mid-tier models deliver optimal performance for any classification workload regardless of latency budgets.
Sonnet with extended thinking enabled, because iterative reasoning strengthens classification robustness across all message types.

explanation: Haiku is the correct choice because this workload demands fast inference with minimal reasoning complexity—spam detection uses simple binary or categorical decisions that don't require the extended reasoning capabilities of larger models. Opus and Sonnet would incur unnecessary latency and cost, while extended thinking would further slow throughput without improving accuracy on straightforward classification tasks. Haiku's design prioritizes speed and efficiency for exactly this use case.

question: You are establishing quality assurance procedures that span from initial design through production deployment. Which two activities strengthen continuity across the project lifecycle? Each correct answer presents a complete solution. (Select two.)

options.text: Develop a stakeholder communication plan and trigger updates whenever major milestones are reached.
Reuse the test suite and baseline dataset across development cycles rather than creating new ones for each iteration.
Store all intermediate work products in archival systems to maintain a complete historical record.
Document insights and recommendations from each stage and feed them into planning for subsequent stages.
Finalize all technical decisions early in the process and prevent any reconsideration once later phases commence.

explanation: Options B and D represent practices that ensure meaningful continuity and knowledge transfer across phases. B preserves evaluation consistency by maintaining the same test framework and reference data, enabling accurate comparison of improvements over time. D captures institutional knowledge from each phase, preventing redundant work and enabling informed decisions in subsequent phases. Options A, C, and E are either too narrow (A), focused on storage rather than active continuity (C), or actively harmful to iterative improvement (E).

question: A financial forecasting tool has exceeded its monthly budget by 42 percent. Analysis reveals three cost drivers: a 5,500-token compliance notice included in every request (48 percent of overage), database lookups returning 2,800 tokens per request (28 percent), and use of a premium model tier (24 percent). The business requires forecast quality to remain at current levels. Which two measures should you prioritize to bring costs down while preserving quality? Each correct answer presents part of the solution. (Select two.)

options.text: Reduce the quantity of database records fetched in each lookup operation.
Shorten the compliance notice by removing boilerplate text that is not legally required.
Implement prompt caching for the static compliance notice across consecutive calls.
Migrate to a lighter Claude model variant for all forecast computations.
Apply response caching to frequently requested forecast scenarios.

explanation: Options C and E are the optimal first steps because they reduce token consumption and API calls without modifying the system logic or model capability. C leverages prompt caching to avoid reprocessing the static compliance notice, directly addressing the largest cost driver (48 percent) while maintaining quality. E caches full responses for repeated queries, reducing both tokens and model invocations for common forecast requests. Options A, B, and D would either require risky modifications to system behavior (A, B) or sacrifice model capability (D) when more efficient optimizations are available.

question: An engineer reports that a newly configured MCP server is not appearing in their Claude Code workspace. What should you recommend as the first troubleshooting action?

options.text: Remove all MCP servers from the configuration file to eliminate competing tool definitions and confirm the environment is clean.
Migrate the team to an alternative Claude product that does not depend on MCP server configurations.
Check that the MCP server appears in the active configuration using the server list command, and restart the session if the server is registered but not visible.
Perform a complete reinstall of the development environment to reset all tool configurations and system state.

explanation: Option C is the correct first step because it performs a minimal, non-destructive diagnostic check that addresses the most common cause: configuration changes require a session restart to take effect. Verifying registration with the list command confirms whether the issue is configuration-related or environmental. Options A, B, and D are unnecessarily destructive—removing all servers eliminates functionality without diagnosis, switching products abandons the current workflow, and reinstalling the OS discards all configuration before any targeted investigation.

question: You are assessing whether a production system requires architectural redesign or can proceed with incremental improvements. Which observation most clearly signals that a redesign phase is necessary?

options.text: A monitoring alert's sensitivity threshold needs fine-tuning to reduce false alarms, which can be addressed through parameter adjustment without modifying system boundaries or service contracts.
An internal process document needs clarification language to help the support team respond faster, which can be handled as a procedural update without affecting how components interact.
A user-visible message contains a grammatical error that should be corrected, which can be resolved as a simple text change without reshaping component responsibilities or interfaces.
The existing system topology cannot satisfy emerging business constraints without restructuring how components interact or altering their foundational agreements.

explanation: Option D correctly identifies a redesign trigger: when the current architecture fundamentally cannot meet new requirements without changing component boundaries or contracts. Options A, B, and C all describe localized, non-structural changes (configuration tuning, documentation clarification, and text correction) that can be handled through operational or content updates without a new design cycle.

question: A healthcare organization is building a patient-record analysis system using Claude and must establish success criteria. The system has two hard constraints: it cannot exceed a spending limit per request, and it must prevent unauthorized personnel from accessing patient information. Which two metrics directly measure compliance with these constraints? (Select two.)

options.text: ROUGE score comparing system-generated summaries to expert-written reference summaries
Percentage of access requests correctly blocked or allowed based on the user's assigned role
Requests successfully completed within a one-minute response window
Actual token consumption per request measured against the maximum allowed budget
Response generation time measured at the 99th percentile across a 30-day operational window

explanation: Options B and D correctly address the two constraints. Option B measures role-based access control enforcement, directly addressing the requirement to prevent unauthorized data access. Option D measures per-request token spend against the budget constraint. Option A measures summary quality (not a stated constraint), Option C measures throughput (not a constraint), and Option E measures latency performance (not a constraint).

question: An architect is preparing architecture documentation for handoff to a development team that will build and deploy a Claude-powered workflow. Which two documentation attributes demonstrate that the package provides sufficient detail for the team to proceed independently? (Select two.)

options.text: The document defines the input schemas, output schemas, and service-level contracts for each system component.
The document includes a traceability matrix showing which architectural decisions were made, what alternatives were considered, and why each alternative was rejected.
The document provides an executive summary of the business problem and the solution's strategic value.
The document lists the architect's name and preferred contact method for resolving ambiguities during implementation.
The document enumerates all candidate models that were evaluated but does not specify which was chosen or justify the selection.

explanation: Options A and B are correct. Option A ensures the team understands what each component must do and how components interact, enabling independent implementation. Option B provides rationale for design decisions, helping the team understand trade-offs and make sound decisions when facing ambiguities. Option C is strategic context (helpful but not sufficient for implementation), Option D creates dependency on the architect (contrary to independence), and Option E withholds critical selection information needed for implementation.

question: An organization is deploying a customer-support chatbot powered by Claude and must establish ethical guidelines for how the system represents itself. Which approach to self-disclosure best upholds responsible and transparent operations?

options.text: Obscure or downplay the AI's involvement in generating responses to increase user perception of authenticity and trust, even though this undermines the user's ability to make informed decisions.
Treat all information about the AI system's role and capabilities as proprietary and decline to answer user inquiries about how responses are produced.
Clearly communicate to end users that responses are generated by AI, consistent with organizational transparency standards, and ensure users can escalate to a human representative when desired.
Inform internal teams and support staff about the AI's role while keeping end users unaware of AI involvement in order to protect operational confidentiality.

explanation: Option C is correct. Transparent disclosure to end users about AI involvement respects user autonomy and informed consent, and providing an escalation path to human support ensures users have recourse. Option A actively deceives users, Option B refuses legitimate transparency, and Option D creates an asymmetry where users cannot make informed decisions about interactions that are materially shaped by AI—violating transparency principles.

question: A solutions architect is preparing to scope a new Claude-powered data analytics platform. Which two activities represent essential elements of thorough discovery and planning before technical design begins? (Select two.)

options.text: Conducting cross-functional sessions with business, operations, and security teams to identify performance targets, quality benchmarks, and regulatory obligations that will inform scope.
Choosing a Claude model variant based on the architect's experience with similar systems before gathering input from stakeholders.
Building a working proof-of-concept and refining it through feedback cycles instead of establishing formal requirements upfront.
Establishing measurable success metrics and clear boundaries for acceptable performance and error rates that will determine readiness for launch.
Postponing the capture of constraints and non-functional requirements until the detailed design phase to prevent premature narrowing of options.

explanation: Options A and D represent structured discovery practices: A emphasizes stakeholder-driven constraint identification across disciplines, while D focuses on defining explicit success criteria and deployment gates. Options B and E represent anti-patterns that skip or delay critical requirements work.
